Task 4: pure typed command schemas — COMMAND_TYPES (exactly 8), one payload dataclass + parser per command type (COMMAND_PAYLOAD_TYPES / COMMAND_PAYLOAD_PARSERS expose the production command_type -> type/parser mappings), CommandEnvelope, RejectedCommand, CommandResult, parse_command(...), canonical_signature(...) for idempotency comparison. parse_command validates an already-typed CommandEnvelope with the exact same field-level rules as a raw mapping (non-empty identifiers, non-negative int-not-bool versions, finite non-negative estimated value, exact payload-type match) rather than passing it through unchecked. _validate_typed_envelope additionally re-runs the payload's own field *values* through the exact same registered COMMAND_PAYLOAD_PARSERS[command_type] parser used for mapping input (by serializing the frozen payload dataclass back to a plain mapping via _to_jsonable) — exact-type matching alone cannot catch a hand-built payload dataclass holding an out-of-enum or out-of-bounds field value (e.g. target_status="TOTALLY-BOGUS"), so this closes that gap and propagates the parser's own RejectedCommand, returning a normalized CommandEnvelope carrying the freshly validated payload (identity-preserved when unchanged, for idempotent re-parsing). ENVELOPE_KEYS and a per-command allowed-payload-key set reject any unrecognized top-level or payload key (including nested relocation/shift-move items); duplicate IDs within a payload's ID collections are rejected before a typed envelope is ever produced. Never mutates input; never raises for business rejections

Task 4: apply_command(...) — parses/dispatches all eight typed commands, optimistic-concurrency version checks, authority-boundary approval gate (hero/value-limit/cross-property/protected-requirement triggers, including room-readiness and maintenance-dispatch cross-property assignment), per-command atomic mutation handlers (_apply_hotel_recovery, _apply_room_readiness_plan, _apply_maintenance_work_order_dispatch, _apply_guest_recovery_action, _apply_booking_inventory_plan, _apply_workforce_shift_plan, _apply_food_beverage_service_plan, _apply_energy_control_plan), command-id idempotency log, typed rejection/acceptance WorldEvents with workflow_id preserved whenever known. Hero relocations require a declared sister-hotel destination (incompatible_property) and emit protected_requirement_breach ahead of the generic incompatible_room reason for protected bookings; hero shift moves and maintenance dispatch resolve the real TeamMember and require engineering skill (skill_mismatch) rather than trusting a denormalized skill field; guest-recovery-action value_gbp must match estimated_value_gbp (value_mismatch) so a mismatched estimate can never bypass the role-limit gate; duplicate entity IDs within a payload collection (rooms_to_restore, relocation booking IDs, shift-move shift IDs, room_ids) are rejected before any mutation. Payload-type guards use explicit checks (never bare assert), safe under python -O Blocking-invariant sync: Hotel.available_<type>_rooms always equals the count of Room entities of that hotel/type with status=="available". select_available_room/select_occupied_room/hotel_available_room_counts/_apply_hotel_availability_deltas are the single source of truth for physical-room selection and per-hotel counter batching (hotel version increments exactly once per command even when multiple relocations/restores/releases touch it). _check_target_versions validates a base/declared target set (no unexpected-key rule); _check_expected_versions additionally rejects any expected_versions key outside the exact final target set as unexpected_expected_version. Hero relocations and booking.inventory-plan.apply now consume a deterministic destination Room (reject insufficient_capacity if none physically exists) and release a deterministic compatible occupied source Room when one exists, before mutating; the 8 hero rooms_to_restore events remain distinct from the new hotel-recovery.room.consumed/released and booking-inventory-plan.room.consumed/released events. room.readiness-plan.apply now explicitly no-ops identical current==target transitions, rejects occupied-room transitions (invalid_room_status), and synchronizes the owning hotel counters/version on every real available<->not_ready transition.
